content: The Continuing Medical Education (CME) program is a collaborative effort between the Duke University Health System Department of Clinical Education and Professional Development and The WikiDoc Foundation. WikiDoc offers an Internet Point-of-Care CME activity, which is a certified educational program allowing physicians to engage in self-directed online learning on topics relevant to their clinical practice. This activity involves a reflective process where physicians document their clinical questions, the sources they consulted, and how the information is applied to their practice. The activity was first posted on November 1, 2015, and expired on November 1, 2016. Each search conducted as part of this activity is estimated to take approximately 30 minutes. Physicians can earn 5 CME credits (AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™) for every cumulative 30 minutes of activity on the WikiDoc website, whether browsing or editing. It has been observed that only about 25% of practitioners implement evidence-based guidelines within seven years of their endorsement by international societies. Furthermore, it can take up to seven years for 50% of physicians in relevant specialties to apply nationally endorsed evidence-based guidelines in their practice. WikiDoc provides healthcare professionals with regularly updated medical information, offering a continuous curriculum that includes the latest medical updates and nationally endorsed evidence-based guidelines. This platform aims to bridge the gap in knowledge dissemination and application by leveraging information technology to promote collaboration and free sharing of medical knowledge among healthcare providers. The rise of medical sub-specialties has led to fragmented care, with limited sharing of expertise across specialties. WikiDoc addresses this issue by enabling healthcare professionals to collaborate, share valuable medical knowledge, and improve both clinical practice and education. The WikiDoc CME activities are designed for various audiences, including: Attending physicians: To enhance their general medical knowledge, prepare for sub-specialty board exams, and assist in teaching residents and medical students. House staff: To prepare for morning reports and as a quick reference while on hospital wards. Medical students: To prepare for morning rounds, research patient conditions, and study for USMLE exams using board review materials. Fellows: To prepare for conferences, teach on hospital wards, and study for specialty board exams. Nursing and ancillary staff: To look up medical information and research patient management, medications, and dosing. Patients: To learn more about their own conditions or those of their family members through the WikiPatient pages. This activity has been planned and implemented by the Duke University Health System Department of Clinical Education and Professional Development and The WikiDoc Foundation to advance patient care. The Duke University Health System Department of Clinical Education & Professional Development is accredited by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME) to provide continuing education for the healthcare team. Physicians should only claim credit proportional to their participation in the activity. There is no limit to the number of Internet Point-of-Care cycles that physicians can complete using WikiDoc. By registering to claim CME credit, physicians' activities on WikiDoc (browsing and editing) will be tracked. Once time is accrued, users can visit the CME Tracker page to monitor their activity. This page provides a log of activities based on the topics browsed, and users can select one or more activities for which they wish to claim CME credit. After verifying their log, users will be prompted to complete a brief survey about the activity. Upon completing the survey, they can print their personalized CME certificate. The following contributors and editors have disclosed no relevant relationships with industry concerning the content of this CME activity: Ochuko Ajari, Turky Alkathery, Robert Badgett, Shanshan Cen, Jyostna Chouturi, Madeleine Cochet, Rebecca Cohen, Yazan Daaboul, Jacquelyne DiTroia, Monalisa Dmello, Laura Goodell, Rim Halaby, Serge Korjian, Tamar Sifri, Kiran Singh, Maria Stepanchak, Ammu Susheela, Omar Toubat, Minu Velan, and Aparna Vuppala. However, the following speakers and planning committee members have disclosed relationships with industry: C. has relationships with Portola Pharmaceuticals, Sanofi-Aventis, Schering-Plough, and The Medicines Company. They are a member of the speakers’ bureau for Daiichi Sankyo, Eli Lilly, St. Jude Medical, and The Medicines Company. They also serve as an independent contractor for Pocket Medicine and UpToDate in Cardiovascular Medicine. The WikiDoc platform is compatible with Internet Explorer 10 or higher, Firefox version 10, and all versions of Google Chrome. Certain content may require additional software to view multimedia, presentations, or printable versions. Required software may include Macromedia Flash, Apple QuickTime, Adobe Acrobat, and Microsoft Office.
